notes.summary: Independent CLD calculus reconstruction with exact degrees and Artinian weights; repairs the invalid strong-positive domination used in 367/368.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves same-open middle-positive decomposition, signed coefficient measures and ordinary scalar compatibility, correct-degree smooth harmonic multiplication and defect support. Checks the exact analytic support theorem. Both factor drafts require a middle-cone repair; source signs and indexing are corrected. No universal Bedford–Taylor assertion is inferred.
notes.text:
Work over any complete non-Archimedean K, including trivial valuation, on an ordinary open N of the original good separated strict boundaryless pure n-dimensional analytic X. T is middle-positive and d'- and d''-closed of bidegree (p,p), 0<=p<=n-1. Put D=d'd'', q=n-p and r=q-1. T acts on compact (q,q)-forms; D(hT) acts on compact (r,r)-forms.

Primary inputs were independently read in the complete preserved CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2 (header 25 July 2025, internal title 29 July 2025). CLD 11.1.7 and 15.7.1–2 supply ordinary analytic domains and canonical calculus over either valuation, without reducedness. Good separated spaces are locally differentially separated by 15.2.2–4. Complete 6.2.4–8 and 15.2.5–9 give prescribed-open compact cutoffs, compact scalar density and finite localization. Only compact localization is used, without assuming global paracompactness. CLD 7.1.1–9 supplies complementary-test currents, smooth wedges, restriction, locality and support.

Concrete correction: on R^4 in degree two, decomposable w satisfy w12*w34-w13*w24+w14*w23=0. Indeed w=a wedge b has w wedge w=0 by repeated factors, whose top coefficient is twice that Plucker expression. The corresponding linear functional of ww^t vanishes on every strongly positive generator and on the standard diagonal order unit, but not on vv^t for v=e12+e34. Therefore strong-positive forms cannot dominate arbitrary symmetric tests. The general strong-domination step in 367/368 and printed CLD 7.2.9 is invalid; PDF page 162 confirms the print. Middle positivity is PSD matrix positivity with the prescribed exterior sign, by 1.2.6. Powers of a positive definite (1,1)-form are interior middle order units by 1.2.13. Bounded coefficients on compact charts admit constant middle domination; finite compact localization proves the needed compact 6.5.2 decomposition.

Thus any compact symmetric (q,q)-test beta supported in an ordinary O subset N has beta=eta_+-eta_- with compact middle-positive outputs in O itself. Extend them by zero to N: compact supports are closed in Hausdorff N and contained in O, so the extensions are smooth. Their supports can exceed supp(beta), but do not leave O.

CLD 7.2.8 and 7.2.11 represent f -> <T,f eta> by a unique positive coefficient Radon measure for positive eta. Their scalar proof bounds f by its supremum times a nonnegative plateau and extends by smooth scalar density. For arbitrary compact diagonal theta, discard its antisymmetric part and subtract measures of its middle-positive decomposition. Uniqueness makes the signed finite measure mu(T,theta) independent of decomposition and supported in supp(theta). CLD 7.2.12's ordinary product is <bT,theta>=integral b dmu(T,theta). Consequently
|<bT,eta_+-eta_->| <= integral |b| dmu(T,eta_++eta_-) <= sup_supp(eta_++eta_-)|b| <T,eta_++eta_->.
Also |<bT,theta>|<=sup_supp(theta)|b|*|mu(T,theta)|(N); this proves fixed-T locally uniform scalar-net continuity.

For smooth beta, <beta wedge(hT),omega>=integral h dmu(T,beta wedge omega). If beta wedge T=0, evaluate on every f omega and use measure uniqueness to conclude beta wedge(hT)=0. If C=gamma wedge T is positive, comparison on all smooth scalars identifies its coefficient measures, proving hC=gamma wedge(hT). Likewise a(hT)=(ah)T for smooth a, and h(aT)=(ha)T for continuous nonnegative a. No continuous product on a general signed current is presumed.

For smooth g, D(gT)=Dg wedge T. On symmetric compact alpha of degree (r,r), set A=g d''alpha-d''g wedge alpha, of type (q-1,q). Leibniz gives Dg wedge alpha-gDalpha=-d'A+C, with C=d'g wedge d''alpha+d''g wedge d'alpha. Jd'=d''J and Jd''=-d'J give JC=-C. Symmetry of T kills C, closedness kills d'A, and <DS,alpha>=<S,Dalpha> proves the identity. Therefore smooth Dg=0 implies D(gT)=0.

If Z is ordinary closed and h continuous, ordinary smooth with zero smooth Hessian off Z, R=D(hT) is symmetric and supported in Z. If chi=1 near Z intersect supp(alpha), <R,alpha>=<R,chi alpha>, because (1-chi)alpha is compact and disjoint from the defect support. No order-zero or positivity premise on R is needed.

The exact CLD 15.2.1 input says a type (a,b) G-form has support in d_K>=max(a,b), and misses a Zariski-closed analytic locus Y in an analytic domain when dim Y<max(a,b). Ordinary forms are G-forms. Its full proof is the tropical chart bound d_trop<=d_K from 12.4.2, then 3.3.6; on Y, d_K<=dim Y. Here d_K is residual transcendence degree plus rational value-group rank, not skeleton dimension.

Actual canonical weights are retained: 13.3.4–7 uses length_A(B)/length_A(A), giving generic degree lambda/mu and 1/mu for nilreduction. Complete 14.4.2 and 15.4.2–3 transport calibration and integration by that degree. Top forms avoid component intersections by 15.2.1, so 16.6.3 gives delta_X=sum m_i delta_(X_i,red) with actual generic Artinian lengths. Positivity follows from calibrated integration; boundaryless Stokes, 7.3.1 and 7.7.4, gives both closedness equations. Our arbitrary T is never reduced or normalized.

Source repairs are explicit in the full manuscript: exterior commutation is (-1)^((a+b)(a'+b')), from generators and 1.3.3, correcting printed 3.3.10 (PDF page 80 inspected); the dk in 3.3.6's proof is dtrop. Only the compact constant-majorant case of 1.10.2 is needed. Misindexed 8.5.3 and 7.7.5 are replaced by correctly typed direct proofs. Recursive Berkovich, dimension/calibration, Radon and Stone-Weierstrass foundations are disclosed rather than newly formalized.

notes.detailedSummary: Uses n1's four calculus lemmas to prove the remaining six items: quantitative bound, weighted-error removal, mass infimum and inverse-oscillation blowup, specified-cover gluing, analytic support removal, and necessary detecting location. Individual finite masses do not imply uniform bounds. ALL369 is correct as conditional partial progress with explicit source repairs, not a solution of the universal atom.
notes.text:
Items 1–4 of whole369 are n1's complete same-open decomposition, product estimate, smooth multiplier identity and defect support. The remaining six items are proved as follows, on the unchanged ambient ordinary open N with arbitrary positive doubly closed T, q=n-p and r=q-1. Assume h continuous and ordinary smooth zero-Hessian off ordinary closed Z.

Item 5. Fix a compact symmetric (r,r)-test alpha and S=Z intersect supp(alpha). In any ordinary O containing compact S choose actual compact smooth 0<=chi<=1, equal to one near S and supported in O. Decompose D(chi alpha)=eta_+-eta_- with middle-positive compact outputs in O and eta=eta_++eta_-. For any smooth g on N with Dg=0, support localization and differential duality give the exact upstairs identity
<D(hT),alpha>=<D(hT),chi alpha>=<(h-g)T,D(chi alpha)>.
Subtracting g is legitimate by n1's smooth identity. Therefore
|<D(hT),alpha>|<=integral |h-g| dmu(T,eta)<=sup_supp(eta)|h-g| <T,eta>.
For empty S take all cutoff forms zero.

Item 6. If every detecting alpha admits a sequence or net of those actual triples with weighted integral tending to zero, the fixed left pairing is zero. Symmetric tests determine the symmetric defect, so D(hT)=0. Supremum error times mass tending to zero is a sufficient stronger premise. Existence of those certificates is not inferred from D[h]=0.

Item 7. Define C_(T,alpha)(S;O) as the infimum of <T,eta_++eta_-> over precisely those actual competitors in O. A competitor exists, so the infimum is nonnegative and finite for each O; it increases as O shrinks. For relatively compact O put omega_g(O)=sup_O|h-g|. Taking the infimum without assuming attainment gives
|<D(hT),alpha>|<=omega_g(O) C_(T,alpha)(S;O).
If h=g on S, continuity and compactness provide small-oscillation neighborhoods. Uniform mass bounds or merely vanishing of this product imply zero. Conversely a detector of magnitude d>0 forces C>=d/omega wherever omega>0 and forbids omega=0. It would force inverse-oscillation mass blowup. Finiteness separately on each neighborhood is not a uniform bound.

Item 8. If these hypotheses and estimates establish zero on members of an ordinary cover of one specified W, restriction and finite compact localization prove zero on W. Only original current identities are glued. A cover is not promoted to a basis.

Item 9. If Z is locally a Zariski-closed analytic locus with dim Z<r, every compact (r,r)-test misses Z by n1's exact CLD 15.2.1 statement. The defect is supported there, so every pairing is zero; locality proves D(hT)=0. The same argument works for ordinary closed Z with the actual pointwise condition d_K(z)<r. Pure codimension c must satisfy c>=p+2. At p=n-1, r=0 and no nonempty locus is excluded. For n=2 the bounds are zero-dimensional at p=0 and none at p=1; for n=3, dimension at most one, at most zero and none.

Item 10. Under off-locus smooth harmonicity alone, a nonzero defect has a compact symmetric detecting test whose support meets Z at a point of d_K>=r. Applying Item 9 with the actual positive doubly closed delta_X proves D[h]=0 when dim Z<n-1, retaining generic Artinian weights. It does not recognize either sign of h as psh or construct admissible U,V. For p>=1, n-p-1<=dim Z<n-1 is an unexcluded dimensional window of this method, not a counterexample; there is no such window at p=0.

notes.summary: Entire 367/368 reconstructed after middle-cone repair: smooth factors of an initial BT current inherit BT exactly when their actual products are positive and doubly closed.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves scalar-measure compatibility and annihilator inheritance, full graded Leibniz for nonclosed hT, elimination of both cross terms and Dgamma, and every-open criteria for an explicit continuous potential class. Scalar nets require each approximant times fixed T closed; common-chart form nets converge to a smooth form. The nonclosed weighted two-torus diagnostic is not a P21.3 counterexample. Submitted factor proofs require correction of the strong-cone step; reconstructed conditional statements hold.
notes.text:
Use n1's repaired coefficient-measure calculus. Let F(O) be a prescribed restriction-compatible class of finite continuous real functions. A positive doubly closed T is BT_F when on every ordinary O and for u,v in F(O) with D[u]=D[v], one has D((u-v)T|O)=0. Initial BT_F is an explicit hypothesis. This can use the original continuous individually psh class without identifying it with generated CPsh.

For any current S and smooth beta of total degree b, signed transposition on compact tests and total exterior commutation give
d'(beta wedge S)=d'beta wedge S+(-1)^b beta wedge d'S,
and likewise for d''. To check signs, move beta past total-degree-m S with (-1)^(bm), transpose differentiation with (-1)^(m+b+1), and expand the smooth derivative of beta wedge omega. No closedness of S is needed. For a smooth (k,k) gamma with 0<=k and p+k<=n (p+k<=n-1 in the original nontrivial testing range), its even total degree gives
D(gamma wedge S)=Dgamma wedge S-d''gamma wedge d'S+d'gamma wedge d''S+gamma wedge DS.

Let T and C=gamma wedge T both be doubly closed, with T positive. First-order Leibniz gives d'gamma wedge T=d''gamma wedge T=0; differentiating the second gives Dgamma wedge T=0. For S=hT, n1's measure uniqueness inherits all three annihilators. Differentiating them with the odd degrees of d'gamma,d''gamma gives
0=-Dgamma wedge S-d'gamma wedge d''S,
0=Dgamma wedge S-d''gamma wedge d'S.
Both cross terms and Dgamma wedge S vanish, proving
D(gamma wedge(hT))=gamma wedge D(hT).
S=hT has not been assumed closed or positive. For a smooth scalar a with aT closed this is D((ah)T)=aD(hT).

If C is positive, n1 identifies the actual ordinary product hC=gamma wedge(hT). Hence, starting from BT_F T, gamma wedge T is BT_F iff the actual product is positive and doubly closed. Necessity belongs to the definition; sufficiency on arbitrary O applies the displayed identity to h=u-v and initial D(hT|O)=0. Gamma itself need not be positive or closed. Closedness of its product is exactly d'gamma wedge T=d''gamma wedge T=0. The scalar criterion is aT BT_F iff the actual product is positive and doubly closed; for a>=0 positivity is automatic.

Scalar-net theorem: if locally smooth nonnegative a_i converge locally uniformly to continuous a and EACH a_iT is closed for the FIXED BT_F T, then aT is positive, closed and BT_F. Fixed coefficient measures give weak convergence and differential convergence. For an admissible h,
<D((a_i-a)hT),omega>=integral(a_i-a)h dmu(T,Domega)->0,
since h is bounded on the fixed compact support and the measure finite. Each earlier identity is zero by the smooth criterion. Continuous associativity follows from n1; locality proves every-open scope. Unrestricted smooth approximation does not preserve this closedness premise.

Form-net theorem: if smooth gamma_i have EACH gamma_i wedge T positive and doubly closed and converge in coefficients on compact supports in a FIXED finite common chart family to a SMOOTH gamma, expand their difference in fixed exterior monomials. Each monomial times a compact test has a finite signed coefficient measure of T. Coefficient convergence proves weak convergence, including tests d'omega and d''omega; positivity passes on positive tests. On Domega multiply coefficients by bounded h and use the same estimate to pass BT. There is no nonsmooth form wedge or changing-moment convergence theorem.

Actual diagnostic: on X=(G_m,Q_l^2)^an, l any prime, set s_j=-log|T_j| and a=2+s1^2>0. X is good separated strict boundaryless pure two-dimensional. Delta_X is positive, doubly closed and tautologically BT_F. But
D(a delta_X)=[2 d's1 wedge d''s1].
For nonzero zeta>=0 smooth compact on R^2, omega=zeta(s) d's2 wedge d''s2 is compact upstairs, supported in a compact polyannulus. The identity moment has finite-flat degree one and calibration one, checked in complete CLD 14.3.1–5, 14.5.3 and 5.8.4. Paired positive orientation gives
<D(a delta_X),omega>=2 integral_R2 zeta ds1 ds2>0.
Thus a delta_X is NOT doubly closed and is excluded from P21.3. This diagnoses the omitted premise in literal CLD 8.6.7, already warned about in the supplied book; it is not imported as a theorem or claimed as a new original counterexample. The companion S=(d's1 wedge d''s1) wedge delta_X is BT_F by the smooth positive closed factor case. Both d'a wedge S and d''a wedge S vanish by repeated generators, so aS is closed and BT_F. Nonconstant relative weights are permitted.

notes.summary: Constructed logarithmic cutoff bounds give analytic-locus smooth-trace removability, including isolated analytic points at every p. Full P21.3 remains unresolved.
notes.detailedSummary: Constructs actual ordinary smooth concave logarithmic truncations, bounds fixed-current curvature K_L<=4LM and energy E_L<=24L²M, and supplies same-neighborhood middle-positive decompositions of mass <=C(F+28M). A local smooth harmonic trace forces weighted errors to vanish without a dimension or assumed capacity bound. Constants provide isolated-point traces, including p=n-1. Also constructs closed approximants for saturated-coordinate torus weights, without arbitrary-current density. Extra off-locus regularity and analytic trace geometry remain unproved universally; candidate=false.
notes.text:
Further independent draft theorem using n1–n3. In the literal original ambient category, let Z be ordinary closed and locally Zariski closed in analytic domains of W. Suppose h is continuous and ordinary smooth with zero smooth Hessian off Z. Suppose each point of Z has an ordinary neighborhood N and ordinary smooth g with Dg=0 and h=g on Z intersect N. Then D(hT)=0 for every positive doubly closed ordinary (p,p)-current, all 0<=p<=n-1. No dimension bound or assumed cutoff-mass bound is imposed. The off-locus and trace hypotheses are substantive, not consequences proved here of D[h]=0.

Complete cutoff proof. Locally take a relatively compact ordinary N inside an affinoid neighborhood, where Z is defined by finitely many analytic f_i (the affinoid noetherian description). Choose a real A larger than all bounded log norms there by at least two. Convolve max(s_1,...,s_m) with a product of nonnegative smooth probability kernels supported in [-1/4,1/4]. The result R_m is smooth convex and differs from max by at most 1/4. A coordinate sufficiently below the others never attains the maximum throughout the kernel support, so it is omitted exactly. This permits coordinates -infinity. Define t=A-R_m(log|f_i|) off Z. Near an individual zero outside Z its coordinate is omitted; the remaining functions are units. Hence t is ordinary smooth in actual unit charts, t>=0, t tends to infinity at Z and Dt<=0, by convexity of R_m applied to affine logarithmic norms. This uses no nontrivial field scaling.

Choose a smooth nondecreasing concave b with b(s)=s on [0,2], constant for s>=4, 0<=b<=4; integrate a nonincreasing smooth derivative from one to zero. Let u_L=L b(t/L), extended by its constant value at Z. Each u_L is ordinary smooth, constant near Z, 0<=u_L<=4L, Du_L<=0, and u_L=t on t<=2L.

Let alpha be any compact symmetric detecting (r,r)-test on N, with K=supp(alpha). Choose finitely many ordinary unit-moment charts U_j covering K, each presenting alpha. On U_j put lambda_j=sum_a d's_(j,a) wedge d''s_(j,a), eta_j=lambda_j^r, with eta_j=1 at r=0. These forms are positive and doubly closed on their respective opens. Choose fixed nonnegative compact smooth rho_j supported in U_j, so at every K-point at least one rho_j is one near it. Such plateaus follow from the compact cutoff theorem. A partition need not have a single global moment presentation. Set M_j=|mu(T|U_j,D rho_j wedge eta_j)|(U_j), F_j=<T|U_j,rho_j lambda_j^q>, M=sum_j M_j, F=sum_j F_j, q=r+1. All are finite. Define
K_(j,L)=<T|U_j,rho_j(-Du_L) wedge eta_j>, E_(j,L)=<T|U_j,rho_j d'u_L wedge d''u_L wedge eta_j>.
Smooth closed-factor duality on U_j gives
K_(j,L)=-<u_LT|U_j,D rho_j wedge eta_j><=4LM_j.
The exact identity D(u_L²)=2u_LDu_L+2d'u_L wedge d''u_L gives
2E_(j,L)=<u_L²T|U_j,D rho_j wedge eta_j>-2<T|U_j,rho_j u_LDu_L wedge eta_j>
<=16L²M_j+8LK_(j,L)<=48L²M_j.
Their sums satisfy K_L<=4LM and E_L<=24L²M. All tests carrying rho_j have compact support inside U_j and extend smoothly by zero to N. The estimates use fixed coefficient measures of the original T.

Take smooth nondecreasing theta=0 on (-infinity,1], theta=1 on [2,infinity). Set v_L=theta(t/L), sigma_L=theta(2t/L), extended as one at Z. With a compact plateau rho1=1 near K, chi_L=rho1 v_L is one near Z intersect K. The actual symmetric beta_L=D(chi_L alpha)=D(v_L alpha) equals
v_LDalpha+d'v_L wedge d''alpha-d''v_L wedge d'alpha+Dv_L wedge alpha.
It is zero on t<=L. Derivatives of v_L are supported on L<=t<=2L, where u_L=t and
Dv_L=L^-1 theta'(t/L)Dt+L^-2 theta''(t/L)d't wedge d''t.

Here is explicit middle domination on each U_j, temporarily writing lambda=lambda_j and eta=eta_j. Fixed compact coefficient bounds give -C lambda^r<=alpha<=C lambda^r and -C lambda^q<=Dalpha<=C lambda^q; coefficients in exterior degrees exceeding the chart dimension are zero. Take a common C for the finite family. For the cross terms temporarily add an independent formal coordinate y representing t. The q-th exterior coefficient space splits into old q-vectors and y wedged with old r-vectors. The symmetric cross term has off-diagonal blocks between these summands. Bounded coefficients and 2|<Av,w>|<=C(|v|²+|w|²), scaling w by 1/L, dominate both signs by C[lambda^q+L^-2 d't wedge d''t wedge lambda^r]. Pullback preserves middle positivity, even if d't is dependent on the old coordinates. On the transition interval, wedge the bound for alpha with positive -Dt and d't wedge d''t to dominate both signs of Dv_L wedge alpha by C[L^-1(-Du_L) wedge eta+L^-2 d'u_L wedge d''u_L wedge eta]. Bounded fixed theta derivatives enter C, independent of L. This is middle PSD domination, not the invalid strong-cone claim.

Therefore, by zero extension of the compact summands, the actual smooth positive form on N
B_L=C sum_j rho_j sigma_L[lambda_j^q+L^-2 d'u_L wedge d''u_L wedge eta_j+L^-1(-Du_L) wedge eta_j]
dominates both signs of beta_L. Wherever beta_L can be nonzero, at least one rho_j sigma_L equals one and that summand dominates both signs; the other summands are positive. Elsewhere beta_L=0. Put eta_(L,±)=(B_L±beta_L)/2. They are actual compact middle-positive forms with difference beta_L and sum B_L. Their supports lie in the fixed compact H=union_j supp(rho_j) and t>=L/2, compact inside the SAME ordinary open O_L={t>L/3} union Z. The strict margin supplies support containment. Positivity and the energy estimates prove the uniform bound
<T,eta_(L,+)+eta_(L,-)><=C(F+L^-2 E_L+L^-1 K_L)<=C(F+28M).

On the fixed compact H, the supports approach Z. For any small-error neighborhood of Z intersect H, the maximum of the finitely many |f_i| has a positive lower bound on its compact complement, so t is bounded above there. Continuity and h=g on Z imply sup_supp(B_L)|h-g|->0. Apply n2's exact cutoff estimate to the actual triple (chi_L,eta_(L,±),g). Every fixed detecting pairing is bounded by this vanishing error times C(F+28M), hence is zero. Finite ordinary localization proves the assertion on W. The proof remains valid at r=0. The cutoff certificates and their uniform masses were constructed rather than assumed.

Corollary: a closed locally zero-dimensional analytic locus is removable in EVERY allowed current degree if h is continuous and ordinary smooth harmonic off it. A zero-dimensional affinoid quotient is Artinian with finite analytic support. Isolate each point z and choose the constant trace g=h(z), then apply the theorem. This includes p=n-1, where 369's dimensional route removed no nonempty locus. Affinoid noetherianity and finite Artinian support are disclosed standard analytic foundations. General ordinary closed skeletons are not thereby analytic loci.

There is also an actual current approximation using n3. On the analytic n-torus over any complete K fix I, |I|=p<=n-1, and S_I=(wedge_(j in I) d's_j wedge d''s_j) wedge delta_X. The initial integration current is tautologically BT; the smooth closed-factor theorem makes S_I positive closed and BT for the original continuous potential class. For continuous A>=0 on R^I, compact nonnegative kernel convolution gives smooth nonnegative A_i converging uniformly on compact sets. Set a_i=A_i(s_I). Each d'a_i wedge S_I and d''a_i wedge S_I is exactly zero by repeated generators. Thus each a_iS_I is positive closed and BT, and n3's fixed-current net theorem gives the actual ordinary product A(s_I)S_I the same property on every ordinary open. Nonsmooth A=|s_1| is included when 1 belongs to I. All identities are upstairs and respect all analytic-unit refinements. This constructs approximants in one displayed family; it supplies no density in arbitrary currents and lies within the catalogue's stated weak closure range.

Full original decision: P21.3 remains unresolved. Neither off-locus ordinary smooth zero-Hessian regularity nor suitable analytic-locus smooth traces are established for all original equal-curvature differences. No general relation-preserving positive doubly closed current exhaustion, differential/cone/ordinary-product-compatible harmonic lift, or admissible analytic X,U,V,T with compact nonzero detector is supplied. Remaining quantifiers are all complete fields including trivial valuation; good separated strict boundaryless pure n>=2 spaces, including singular, reducible and nonreduced; every ordinary open; all p=0,...,n-1; arbitrary positive doubly closed ordinary CLD currents; separately admissible finite continuous individually psh U,V with exact upstairs D[U]=D[V]; and actual Artinian integration weights. No CPsh recognition, two-nonsmooth-factor symmetry, scalar current ascent/descent, or unproved strong-product identification is used. Specified covers remain different from genuine every-open bases. Candidate=false.
